assumption_under_test: For a null gate, each cycle success indicator Xi only satisfies P(Xi=1)<=1/2; dependence across cycles is otherwise arbitrary.

theorem.statement: For n cycle indicators and threshold r>=1, sup P(sum Xi >= r) over all joint laws with P(Xi=1)<=1/2 is min(1,n/(2r)).
theorem.upper_bound: Markov: E[sum Xi] <= n/2, hence P(sum Xi>=r)<=n/(2r), capped at 1.
theorem.sharp_witness: If r<=n/2, always choose a uniformly random r-subset. If r>n/2, with probability n/(2r) choose a uniformly random r-subset and otherwise choose the empty set. Each marginal is <=1/2 and the threshold event attains the bound.

iut_consequence: For the AB-and-CB intersection-union target, under a global null one component may be null and the other deterministically pass. Therefore the same 23/32 worst-case size applies to the frozen r=16 component gate under marginal-only cross-cycle information.
negative_control_note: The AC >=16/23 veto can also fire with probability as high as 23/32 under only marginal cycle validity and arbitrary cross-cycle dependence. Because it is a veto, this inflates false-veto risk rather than false speedup acceptance.

decision.fail_closed_rule: No confirmatory alpha interpretation from the 23-cycle count threshold unless a stronger predeclared cross-cycle joint-law calibration is justified. Independence is sufficient but not logically necessary.

boundary: Finite probability/design audit only; no native CFD timing, speedup, PDE theorem, Working Truth/Foundation promotion, or final acceptance.
